TITLE: The AI trade gets a reappraisal
CONTENT:
The article says the AI boom is entering a phase described as “rational exuberance,” with investors pulling back funding and seeking more evidence that investments will pay off. It frames the issue as whether investors can reduce bubble-like expectations without undermining the broader AI-driven economy. It states investors still expect long-term AI to deliver productivity gains, but notes reduced mania.

It cites signs of retreat across different parts of the AI buildout: neocloud companies are described as being hit hardest due to heavy borrowing and reliance on Big Tech backing to build data centers and sell computing power; bond investors are said to demand more compensation for lending to neoclouds, with CoreWeave cited. It mentions Elice’s stock plunging more than 30% in its trading debut and Firmus shelving a planned IPO after investors balked at its valuation. It reports that Nvidia may invest hundreds of millions in Firmus, and notes that chip stocks have slid since the Nasdaq peak on Oct. 6. It also says hyperscalers (Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet) moved from using cash stockpiles to borrowing and that investors are adjusting. The text includes a quote indicating hyperscalers initially financed via free cash flow and are now moving into credit markets, which is described as having an “indigestion period.” It concludes that Wall Street still believes AI will transform markets and the economy.

TITLE: Nvidia reveals plans for 'an AI factory in a shipping container' to build data centers in weeks, not months
CONTENT: Nvidia says it wants to reduce the time it takes customers to start generating revenue from its AI systems. At its GTC event in Berlin, the company unveiled DSX POD, described as a reference design for an AI data center in a shipping-container-sized box. The article says traditional data center construction can take months to years and that delays increase expenses because revenue generation starts when AI systems begin processing tokens. DSX POD is presented as a faster, modular approach intended to reduce deployment time from six months to 14 days. The article states DSX PODs are meant to arrive on site and be ready to plug into existing power, cooling, and networking infrastructure, and that they are not intended to replace traditional data centers but to enable running AI applications before full facilities are ready. Nvidia also states DSX POD supports liquid cooling and can save up to 54 million liters of water per day versus a standard data center. The article notes Nvidia plans to deliver DSX POD with partners including Anduril, Armada, Bull, Crusoe, Dell Technologies, Foxconn, and others starting in early 2027, and suggests faster deployment may help address AI infrastructure bottlenecks such as power and chip sales.

TITLE: People are now recognizing Nvidia's compute has a great deal of residual value,' CEO Jensen Huang tells Deirdre Bosa
CONTENT: In an interview, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said Wall Street is recognizing the usefulness of using Nvidia hardware as collateral to finance data center expansion. He said Nvidia processors have long-term value that can backstop debt tied to constructing data centers. Huang discussed Nvidia’s ability to use its GPU hardware as a financial instrument, and referenced Nvidia’s agreement in August to create a $500 billion funding pool with six financial institutions. He also said Nvidia’s computing systems are productive for a long time due to widespread use and software upgradability, and described how customer demand for older architectures illustrates longer asset lifecycles. He said the compute is productive, fungible, and durable, and could allow underwriting loans against the asset itself.

He discussed the idea of extending to the local community, sharing what the project will bring, and tailoring benefits to community needs.

The article says data center construction has faced opposition in parts of the US, including bans and moratoriums, and mentions New York’s statewide one-year moratorium and Texas pausing aspects of grid connections for new data centers. It also describes political debate and residents’ complaints related to noise, water usage, and electricity costs.

He also added that companies should be “good visitors” and “good guests,” and stop by to see how they can be helpful before going into a community.

TITLE: Quest Diagnostics Data Breach Investigation: Edelson Lechtzin LLP Probes Class Action Claims After Unauthorized Access to Patient Records
CONTENT: NEWS PROVIDED BY Edelson Lechtzin LLP. The article says Edelson Lechtzin LLP is investigating data privacy claims arising from an alleged data breach at Quest Diagnostics. It states that Quest identified unauthorized access to its Quanum Lab Services Manager system on October 21, 2026, and that an unauthorized party accessed certain patient records disclosed in a Form 8-K filed on October 22, 2026. The article says Quest notified federal law enforcement, engaged third-party cybersecurity experts, and initiated its incident response, including implementing remedial measures and temporarily pausing access to the system while it investigates. It describes the potentially exposed information as patient records/protected health information, health and medical records in the Quanum platform, and related diagnostic, test-result, and billing data, noting that the full scope is still being investigated. It also describes who may be affected (patients whose personal and health information was maintained in the Quanum system) and says the company has not yet stated how many patients were affected. It includes an overview of legal options, stating the firm evaluates claims at no cost, and lists recommended steps such as watching for notices, placing fraud alerts/credit freezes, and reviewing financial and benefits statements. The article provides contact information for a case evaluation and includes an “About Edelson Lechtzin LLP” section.

TITLE: AI Debt Fears Leads Investors To Seek Safer Havens. The 10-Year Treasury Yield Slipped Below 5%
CONTENT: Investors sought shelter in U.S. government bonds as concerns about AI infrastructure debt financing rattled technology stocks, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield below 5% for the first time in a month. The yield was near 4.99% on Friday, up about 3 basis points for the session but still below the threshold breached Thursday. The article describes a reversal from earlier in the month when yields rose to the highest levels in more than two decades. It says investors are weighing risks in the AI trade against persistent inflation pressures and notes CoreWeave as a focal point, with its shares falling 10% Thursday and down 38% for October. It reports CoreWeave’s 9.75% bond maturing in 2031 reaching 15.72% and a five-year credit default swap spread of 1,138 basis points. The article mentions the Fed’s upcoming meeting and market expectations regarding the benchmark rate, and summarizes economic and energy updates including consumer sentiment details, S&P Global’s PMI, WTI and Brent futures levels, and reports about attacks on Saudi oil installations. It also notes other Treasury maturities edging higher on Friday.

TITLE: Update: Equities Mostly Lower Intraday as Oil Prices Soar
CONTENT: (Updates with latest market prices and developments.) Wall Street’s benchmark equity indexes were lower intraday as fears of a re-escalation in the Middle East conflict sent US crude oil prices soaring past $100 a barrel again. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 1.2% at 52,238.5 after midday Friday, while the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,629.7, and the Nasdaq Composite edged down 0.1% to 25,984. Except energy and technology, all sectors were in the red, led by consumer staples. West Texas Intermediate crude oil was up 3.6% to $103.08 a barrel intraday, and Brent jumped 2.9% to $116.46. Iran’s military is reported as fully prepared for “asymmetric warfare.” The article also mentions reports that the US and Israel have drawn up plans to resume military operations against Iran after November midterm elections, and that Iran-aligned Houthi rebels have continued to strike Saudi Arabia. It states that Treasury yields were higher intraday, with the 10-year rate up to 4.99% and the two-year rate up to 4.67%. It reports that US consumer sentiment dropped to its lowest level in five months and that US private-sector growth eased while employment increased and selling prices rose, based on data referenced from a University of Michigan survey and S&P Global’s flash purchasing managers’ index. In company news, it says American Express reported third-quarter revenue just below Wall Street expectations and that its chief executive disclosed plans to terminate about 5% of its global workforce; it also states that SLB reported better-than-expected third-quarter results and that Deckers Outdoor slumped 5.5%. It additionally notes that spot gold dipped and silver lost.

TITLE: Apple Is Up 28% This Year: Take Profits, or Hold On for the Ride?
CONTENT: Apple’s stock is reported as up 28% this year and at record highs, with the article stating Apple has matched the entire technology sector while Microsoft and Alphabet are behind. It says the company’s newly launched iPhone Duo is driving momentum, with early demand described as solid, though the iPhone Duo is reportedly in short supply. The article also mentions that Apple’s services business adds recurring revenue on top of device sales. It compares Apple’s year-to-date performance to Microsoft and Alphabet, and notes Apple’s weight in ETFs including the Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY). The article frames a decision for shareholders around taking profits versus holding, and says holiday-quarter results and iPhone Duo demand and availability will be important. It includes references to overlap with index fund exposure through holdings in XLK and SPY.

TITLE: Netflix Is Now Down 29% This Year: Is NFLX Stock Hopeless or Ready for a Rebound?
CONTENT: The article discusses Netflix’s stock performance, noting it is down 29% year to date to $66.29 despite a Q3 earnings beat. It says a cut to advertising-related guidance spooked investors and that the stock is down further compared with benchmarks. It compares Netflix’s performance with Roku, which is up 47% year to date, and briefly contrasts with Walt Disney, which is down 1% in 2026 so far. The article summarizes Netflix’s Q3 results, including GAAP earnings per share and operating margin expansion, and describes management’s Q4 revenue forecast and advertising revenue outlook changes. It also states Netflix’s rebound depends in part on expanding its ad-supported tier into 15 new countries in 2027 and that 2027 guidance will be issued with its fourth-quarter report. It mentions Netflix also bought back $4.8 billion of its stock during the quarter and provides additional commentary on operating income, free cash flow guidance, and guidance pressure related to job cuts.

TITLE: Amazon Survived a 50% Crash. Here’s What a $1,000 Investment Became
CONTENT: The article discusses Amazon’s performance over the past decade, stating it survived a 50% stock drop, a CEO transition, and its first losing year in nearly a decade before recovering. It describes growth in AWS and mentions that AWS revenue rose 36.7% to $42.2 billion in Q2 2026, and that advertising revenue was $19.8 billion in Q2 2026 (up 26%). It notes Amazon expected $220 billion in 2026 capex and that trailing free cash flow was negative at -$7.6 billion. It includes return figures showing a $1,000 investment in AMZN 10 years ago becoming $5,966, with the article providing 1-year, 5-year, and 10-year return tables. The text also covers timing of purchases around AWS/Prime growth, a 2022 decline, and discusses expectations for future earnings and spending/capex. It ends with a promotional section about a report from 24/7 Wall St. and includes contact information.

TITLE: Apple is set to take back the market-cap crown from Nvidia. Upcoming earnings may push it over the top
CONTENT: The article says Apple is set to take back the market-cap crown from Nvidia, and that upcoming earnings may push it over the top.

TITLE: AbbVie’s Dividend Survived Humira’s Patent Cliff. Will Merck and Amgen’s?
CONTENT:
The article discusses how dividend safety may be affected when major drugs lose patent protection (patent cliffs). It compares AbbVie, Merck, Amgen, and Gilead based on newer drugs replacing older ones, dividend coverage, free cash flow, and related risk factors.

AbbVie: The piece says AbbVie yields 2.3% and describes quarterly dividend levels and historical increases, discusses dividend safety using trailing and adjusted EPS and free cash flow, and notes net leverage and negative book equity tied to the Allergan deal. It provides figures for Humira declines and growth for Skyrizi and Rinvoq, including patent-related timing for Skyrizi.

Merck: The piece describes Merck’s dividend level and history of increases, addresses concerns about trailing EPS versus the dividend and suggests the gap reflects one-time charges. It cites KEYTRUDA sales and upcoming loss of exclusivity, and outlines growth drivers and risks related to expected moderation in U.S. KEYTRUDA growth.

Amgen: The article states Amgen yield and dividend increase history, discusses dividend coverage by EPS and free cash flow, and provides sales trends for certain products. It highlights growth drivers and mentions debt as a risk factor.

Gilead Sciences: The piece discusses Gilead’s lower yield, a GAAP net loss attributed to acquired R&D write-offs, and free cash flow used for dividends and buybacks. It contrasts Veklury’s decline with ongoing HIV sales growth and mentions upcoming FDA decisions.

The article concludes with a ranking of the four dividends by “patent-cliff readiness,” stating none of the four show classic warning signs of a dividend cut while summarizing the main concerns and supports for each company.

TITLE: What To Expect From Wednesday’s Federal Reserve Meeting
CONTENT: The article says the Federal Reserve’s policy committee is likely to keep its key interest rate steady when it meets on Wednesday. It notes that economists expect potential future rate increases to address high inflation, but do not expect an immediate second consecutive rate hike after September’s increase. It discusses how higher rates can raise borrowing costs, dampen inflation, and potentially slow the economy, while also affecting the job market. It states markets were pricing in a one-in-ten chance of a quarter-point rate hike, referencing CME Group’s FedWatch tool. It also covers recent discussions by Fed officials about whether to follow up on September’s hike, mentions the Fed’s inflation and employment objectives, and says many experts expect a rate increase in December. The article further describes how a pause in October could give officials more time to assess inflation impacts related to the Iran war’s fuel price effects, and references comments by Fed officials suggesting they did not favor back-to-back rate hikes.

TITLE: SpaceX Filing Gives Elon Musk the Final Word on Tesla Merger He Says He’s Staying Out Of
CONTENT: The article says Elon Musk recused himself from the SpaceX-Tesla merger talks, and that a SpaceX SEC filing suggests this does not change his influence. It states SpaceX’s October 22 10-Q says any potential combination with Tesla would require further approval by the special committee, the board of directors, and the controlling shareholder, and that Musk controls roughly 85% of SpaceX’s voting power as the controlling shareholder. The article describes that special committees were formed on October 20 to evaluate a proposed deal estimated to create a combined entity worth around $3.5 trillion, and quotes Musk describing staying out as an “odd kabuki dance” where he cannot be in the conversation, while noting the filing language suggests he will have the last word. It mentions a Reuters report that Musk’s earlier public endorsement created complications for the independent process and the committees’ ability to negotiate at arm’s length. The article also notes critics point to Tesla’s 2016 SolarCity acquisition as a governance precedent and says SpaceX investor disclosures flagged Musk’s overlapping interests as a material risk. It states Tesla shareholders must clear a threshold of 50% of all outstanding shares, not a simpler majority of votes cast, and quotes Musk calling it a “quite a high hurdle.” It adds that Tesla’s annual meeting is December 3.

TITLE: AEP and Xcel Energy Face Surging Power Demand. Which Dividend Is Safer?
CONTENT: The article compares American Electric Power (AEP) and Xcel Energy (XEL) as regulated utilities facing new demand from data centers and discusses their dividend outlooks. It states that both utilities yield about 3% and point to earnings growth, but it argues the difference is what could put the dividend at risk. It reports past one-year performance, compares the latest dividend raises and targeted annual increases, and contrasts dividend coverage as a share of earnings versus each company’s target range. It also describes AEP’s contracted load additions and $78 billion capital plan versus Xcel’s smaller data center pipeline and retained 2026 guidance. The piece highlights risk factors it attributes to Xcel, including wildfire-related costs, litigation, debt and a negative credit outlook, and compares these to AEP’s disclosures about regulatory issues and targets for funds-from-operations-to-debt and planned equity. It concludes with a verdict that AEP’s dividend is “built to last,” while Xcel’s slightly higher yield comes with wildfire and credit-related risks.

TITLE: Consumer sentiment dips on worries about affordability: UMichigan survey
CONTENT:
The article says consumer sentiment inched down this month, with worries that persistent inflation will weaken buying power. It reports that household perceptions of conditions for purchasing durable goods slumped 18% due to concerns about rising interest rates and declining affordability. It also states that the decline in sentiment among independent voters exceeded increases in outlook among Republicans and Democrats. It includes quotes from Joanne Hsu, noting that purchasing power dominates consumer views and that sentiment has fallen since just before the start of the U.S. war with Iran.

It further reports that selling prices rose at the fastest rate since Aug. 2022, citing an S&P Global survey of purchasing managers, and includes comments about cost pressures, supply chain bottlenecks, and backlogs prompting companies to raise prices. The article mentions that Fed officials are scheduled to discuss monetary policy on Oct. 27–28, and it provides figures on Brent crude oil prices and inflation expectations for a year from now and for the long run, including quotes from Hsu about above-target inflation and potential entrenchment of elevated expectations.

TITLE: Scalpers offer Apple iPhone Duo buyers hundreds extra outside Beijing launch
CONTENT: The article says Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo was launched globally on Friday. It describes scalpers outside the Beijing flagship Apple store in Sanlitun offering to buy newly purchased Duo phones on the spot for hundreds of dollars more. The piece also references that China is the world’s largest market for foldable phones, and includes comments from people waiting in line and trying to purchase the device, along with additional context about other companies’ foldable launches. It also mentions expectations around Apple Intelligence features and related regulatory timelines and availability in China.

TITLE: Sherwin Williams (SHW) Faces Higher Earnings Expectations, Is It Trading At An 11% Discount?
CONTENT: The article says Sherwin-Williams (SHW) reaffirmed its income stream by declaring a quarterly dividend of $0.80 per share payable on December 4, 2026, with an ex-dividend and record date of November 13. It states that Wall Street projects higher earnings per share and revenue for the upcoming quarter. It reports the share price reaction as positive, noting SHW is up 2.5% over the last day and has a 5.3% 30-day share price return, with a 1-year total shareholder return of 5.2% and a 3-year total shareholder return of 49.3%. It says the dividend news and the recent share price move place the stock near the middle of its valuation range, about 10% below average analyst targets and roughly 13% below one intrinsic value estimate. It includes a “Most Popular Narrative: 11% Undervalued,” stating Sherwin-Williams is trading at $345.63 with fair value pegged at $389.09, and references a 7.57% discount rate. It mentions a plan to open 80 to 100 net new Sherwin-Williams Paint Stores Group locations each year to reach roughly 6,000 stores, alongside pruning of underperforming sites. It lists potential risks such as raw material inflation tightening margins or weak DIY and construction demand lingering. It also states another valuation view from DCF work, saying the stock trades about 13.2% below an intrinsic value estimate of $398.06, and notes the current P/E is roughly 31x compared with Chemicals industry and peer averages.

TITLE: Is Earnings Optimism Altering The Investment Case For Hershey Stock (HSY)?
CONTENT: The article discusses Hershey’s outlook amid expectations for higher earnings and revenue in the September 2026 quarter. It notes that management is leaning on heavier brand spending and product launches across chocolate and snacks. It highlights Dot’s Homestyle Pretzels, acquired in 2021, as a lead salty snack platform and says there are plans to move beyond pretzels into broader snack categories and new mixes by 2027. It frames an “investment narrative” around whether Hershey can convert brand spending and a broader snack portfolio into healthier volumes, discusses operational risks including pricing power and potential capacity or freight issues, and references concerns such as volume decline, U.S. chocolate share loss, and higher leverage. The article states the upcoming September 2026 earnings report expectations of US$2.12 in EPS and US$3.25b in revenue. It also describes Hershey’s investment plans including automation in salty snacks, expanded capacity into 2027, and an innovation slate in chocolate and Dot’s led snacks. It presents a longer-range forecast of US$13.1b in revenue and US$2.1b in earnings by 2029, based on assumptions of 2.6% yearly revenue growth and increased earnings from US$1.5b today.

TITLE: Learn Why The Bull Case For Illinois Tool Works Stock Could Change Following Quarterly Earnings Preview
CONTENT: The article says Illinois Tool Works is set to report September quarter results, with analyst forecasts of $2.99 per share earnings and $4.26 billion revenue versus the same quarter a year earlier. It highlights Test & Measurement and Electronics and Welding as key segments expected to deliver double digit year-over-year growth and shape the earnings mix. It discusses an investment narrative focused on a steady industrial portfolio and enterprise cost programs, noting the September quarter preview supports the thesis but does not radically change it. It also mentions near-term execution in capex-heavy areas, potential margin pressure risks if price increases lag input costs or if weaker Food Equipment and Specialty Products trends deepen, and management’s emphasis on enterprise initiatives adding about 120 basis points to operating margin in Q1 and Q2 2026. It further notes earlier in 2026 that Welding and Test & Measurement and Electronics posted double digit organic growth, orders ahead of revenue, and that newer products contributed 3% to first half sales. The article includes a narrative tied to revenues of US$18.4b and earnings of US$3.8b by 2029, based on 3.8% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$0.6b from earnings today of roughly US$3.2b.

TITLE: ‘Window of vulnerability’: Banks move to restrict AI agent access
CONTENT: The article says multiple banks, including Citi Bank, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and JPMorgan Chase, have taken steps to limit third-party AI agents from accessing their platforms and services. It notes the concern that AI agents could take unwanted actions on behalf of users and cites a 2026 Palo Alto Networks study about agentic AI being a leading cybersecurity risk. A Citi spokesperson is quoted saying third-party AI agents or assistants are not permitted to log into a customer’s account or transact directly within Citi’s digital banking platforms, while customers may authorize agents to limited, read-only access to account information with certain Citi-approved open banking providers. The article also includes a quote about a “window of vulnerability” as AI is weaponized, and it describes consumer concern cited from a Ping report about AI agents misrepresenting personality or values. It further states that Bank of America, Capital One, and other global banks created a coalition in September to warn about agentic technology moving faster than protections, highlighting risks related to AI shopping agents and emphasizing the need for human involvement before payments.

TITLE: Wall Street closes lower to end rocky week
CONTENT: Wall Street closed lower on Friday as technology shares steadied, ending a turbulent week tied to the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite posted a small loss after its biggest one-day drop since June, with concerns about financing costs for heavy AI investment. The S&P 500 technology sector rose 0.35%, while most S&P 500 sectors fell, including consumer staples, consumer discretionary, and financials. Next week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies are set to report results, including Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 652.82 points (1.23%), the S&P 500 lost 39.75 points (0.52%), and the Nasdaq Composite fell 53.52 points (0.21%). For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.7%, while the Dow rose 0.4% for its third straight weekly gain. The communication services sector was pressured by declines in telecommunications stocks after a report about SpaceX seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier. The energy sector rose 2.5% to a record high, and American Express shares fell 3.7% after raising its profit forecast and announcing plans to eliminate 5% of its workforce. SLB shares rose after beating Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit, and US consumer sentiment edged down near a record low in October according to the University of Michigan.

TITLE: Moderna stock extends losses as investors digest melanoma vaccine trial data
CONTENT: The article says Moderna (MRNA) extended losses on Friday after a sharp sell-off the previous session as investors digested data from a late-stage trial of its personalized melanoma vaccine. It notes the stock closed down more than 1% a day after plunging more than 17% in its worst single-day performance since Aug. 20, and that more than $17 billion in market value vanished on Thursday as late-stage trial details circulated ahead of the official debut. It states that Merck (MRK), Moderna’s partner, confirmed results came out early and that full data is set for release on Saturday at Europe’s biggest cancer conference in Madrid. The article also mentions that the leaked figures did not initially impress Wall Street and cites analyst rating/price target statements from Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Citi, and a summary of buy/hold/sell ratings. It further notes that the company’s valuation has shifted over the summer away from declining COVID-19 vaccine business toward potential in cancer treatment, and references August phase 3 results for its personalized cancer vaccine developed with Merck.

TITLE: Exclusive: Meta acquires AI data platform Sundial
CONTENT: Meta has acquired Sundial, an AI-powered data analytics platform. The platform was founded by two former Meta employees, and a spokesperson confirmed the acquisition to Axios. Sundial will be folded into Meta’s new data analytics organization. Sundial co-founders Julie Zhuo and Chandra Narayanan will join Meta. Other Sundial employees, including Meta alumni, will also join, and Sundial will stop serving external customers when the deal closes. The Sundial platform allows businesses to get quick access to reliable data analysis, turning natural-language questions and complex data into simpler, actionable insights via a chatbot plugin. The article also mentions that Meta named Alex Schultz as its first-ever chief data officer in July, and that he leads a Data Analytics Tooling & Agents unit (DATA) responsible for descriptive analysis, experimentation, monitoring critical AI systems, and issuing alerts.

TITLE: The AI sell-off is crushing stocks of companies leading the data center build-out
CONTENT: The article says that despite “blowout quarters,” two major suppliers to the AI data center build-out are being sold off by investors. It reports that Bloom Energy (BE) said sales jumped 138% last quarter and raised its full-year outlook to roughly 122% growth; and Comfort Systems (FIX) said its backlog nearly doubled to $17.8 billion. It states that Bloom and Comfort Systems fell again Friday, and that Credo (CRDO) also fell. The piece also cites Yahoo Finance calculations that since the S&P 500’s Oct. 6 record close, the companies building and equipping AI data centers are down a median 23%, including Caterpillar (CAT), GE Vernova (GEV), Vertiv (VRT), and Eaton (ETN). It includes comparisons that power producers are down 14%, Nvidia (NVDA) is off 11%, and Big Tech is down 5%. The article discusses commentary that power is the biggest constraint for the AI build-out, and includes discussion of supply vs. demand for computing power and transformer lead times, noting concern about a possible “scarcity unwinds.” It also states that a dozen of the biggest builders and power names have shed more than $300 billion in market value since Oct. 6.

TITLE: Meta stock closes out Friday down as AI spending fears continue to rattle markets
CONTENT:
Meta (META) stock closed out Friday down roughly 1%, after Thursday shares plunged 7%. The article says Meta reported better-than-anticipated Q3 revenue, but AI spending fears and renewed concerns about whether AI data center investments will pay off led investors to pull back on AI-related stocks.

It states Meta raised the lower end of its capital expenditure estimate to $135 billion to $145 billion (from $130 billion to $145 billion) and also has $825 billion in various spending commitments tied to cloud capacity arrangements, energy service agreements, and consumer hardware products. It notes analysts were largely bullish due to prospects for its Muse AI agent and models.

The article says CEO Mark Zuckerberg highlighted Muse’s profitability over multiple years, contingent on improving compute efficiency. It reports Q3 revenue of $64 billion (vs. $63.3 billion anticipated) and GAAP earnings per share of $3.83 (vs. $3.56 expected), mentioning legal charges related to a teen mental health settlement.

It also says Meta will issue new nonvoting Class C shares to all Class A stockholders, effectively creating a 2-for-1 stock split, and that a New Mexico judge ordered the company to pay $25 billion related to a consumer-harms case. The article references a proposal (Proposition 40) described as a 5% tax on taxpayers with assets over $1 billion.

TITLE: Earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally
CONTENT: US stock investors face a pivotal week as corporate earnings reports led by major AI players and a Federal Reserve meeting pose tests for a market rally. Weakness in technology shares has left investors concerned about the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss on Friday after its biggest daily drop since June, following disappointing quarterly reports from Meta and Lam Research. Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon are set to headline the next round of quarterly results, along with a large portion of S&P 500 companies. The Fed’s interest rate policy meeting on Wednesday could also rattle markets. Investors are also focused on the November 3 midterm elections. The article notes robust US profit growth and that third-quarter S&P 500 earnings are on pace to rise more than 32% year over year, with next week described as the busiest earnings week.

TITLE: How Upcoming Earnings At FirstEnergy (FE) Has Changed Its Investment Story
CONTENT: The article says FirstEnergy is set to report third quarter 2026 results after the market close on 27 October. It states that performance will be shaped by data center and industrial power demand, alongside rising operation, maintenance, and storm restoration costs. It says the earnings release will focus on how effectively FirstEnergy’s Energize365 grid modernization spending translates into returns while offsetting a heavier cost base. The article also discusses how the investment narrative depends on regulated grid and transmission investment matching rising electricity demand from data centers and industrial users, highlighting Energize365 projects improving reliability and capacity while data center load ramps. It mentions that the short-term catalyst is how management ties data center demand and grid upgrades to recoverable rate base growth, and the risk is that higher O&M and storm restoration expenses, combined with heavy capital spending, could pressure free cash flow and customer bill affordability. It states that the capital plan around Energize365 reaffirms $6b earmarked for 2026 and a broader $36b program through 2030. It also describes analyst forecasts, including 4.9% yearly revenue growth for the next three years and higher profitability as regulated projects come through.

TITLE: Will Earnings Beat Change Dow (DOW) Narrative
CONTENT: Dow Inc. reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$11.27b and net income of US$458m, with earnings per share ahead of analyst expectations. The quarter highlights Dow’s pricing actions and cost savings programs contributing to higher earnings, while the firm continues a century long dividend record. The article states that Dow’s “self help” plan in costs and portfolio mix is supported by the reported numbers at an operating level, and identifies near-term factors as execution on US$1.3b of planned self help benefits and a broader US$3b structural program, alongside managing energy and raw material pressures. It describes margin risk from elevated input costs and softer polyethylene demand as an operational overhang even after the earnings beat. It also mentions catalysts and stated targets for US$700m of growth and productivity benefits in 2026 and about US$2b of uplift by 2027, and discusses how better-than-expected earnings could affect debt reduction, funding of projects, and dividend support while tracking interest coverage and litigation risks. It summarizes an analyst framework involving gradual revenue growth, forecasts of 2.3% revenue growth per year over the next three years, and a shift from loss to mid single digit profit margins, including a consensus view of earnings moving from a current loss of US$1.3b to US$2.1b by 2029.

TITLE: Stocks fall, but tech shares steady after selloff; oil hits highest in nearly six months
CONTENT: Major stock indexes ended lower on Friday as tech shares mostly steadied. The Nasdaq eased and European shares also ended lower. An index of semiconductors rose 0.4%, and the S&P 500 technology index was also up 0.4%. The S&P 500 energy sector rose 2.5% to a record high, with Brent crude futures settling at $116.72 per barrel and US West Texas Intermediate closing at $103.27 per barrel, both up on the day. US Treasury yields rose after the benchmark 10-year yield posted its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years. Investor focus remained on earnings season, and next week’s quarterly results for Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon were noted. Meta shares ended down 1%, while Microsoft was up 0.7%. Shares of Alphabet and Amazon eased. American Express shares fell 3.7% after results and remarks from its CEO. Telecom company shares including Verizon dropped after a report about SpaceX being in talks with cellular infrastructure companies about launching a US wireless carrier program.

TITLE: France spared Moody's ratings downgrade as it struggles with unrest
CONTENT: Moody's concluded a periodic review and kept France's credit rating at Aa3 with a negative outlook, easing pressure on the government. The article says bond markets had priced in a downgrade. The French finance ministry attributed the unchanged rating to the credibility of the 2027 finance bill and its plan to keep public finances on a recovery path. It describes challenges passing the bill in parliament and notes that opposition parties could reject it and potentially topple the government. Moody's said the Aa3 rating assumes adoption of a deficit-reducing 2027 budget and that financing costs and social tensions will ease. The article also discusses borrowing costs, investor concerns about the budget deficit and upcoming elections, and the impact of protests and riots on political and fiscal efforts. It adds that Moody's previously identified parliamentary fragmentation as key to its next rating move and mentions the status of savings measures and proposed deficit targets in the 2027 budget.

TITLE: Moody’s holds steady on France’s credit rating as country grapples with turmoil and higher yields
CONTENT: Moody’s decided to maintain its credit rating on France. The agency kept France’s credit rating at Aa3 and maintained its negative outlook. The decision came as France dealt with a week of civil unrest and rising political risk, and investors had been anticipating the rating decision amid a surge in bond yields, with the 10-year bond yield surpassing 5% for the first time since 2002.

TITLE: Bunge (BG) Stock May Be Below Fair Value On Earnings Power
CONTENT: The article discusses Bunge Global’s stock valuation relative to its earnings power. It notes the stock’s recent closing price of US$103.22 and describes shareholders’ multi-year return and the question of how much of that gain is reflected in the earnings multiple. It mentions that factors such as pricing power, cost control, and execution influence an appropriate P/E. It also compares the stock’s roughly 19.6x earnings multiple to the broader food industry average (about 18.6x) and a peer group (closer to 23.2x), characterizing the valuation as a middle ground. The piece states that a fair value framework suggests a higher P/E than the market is assigning and frames the resulting gap as raising questions about whether the market is pricing more risk than the model implies or whether the model is overly generous about business quality. It references the “Simply Wall St Narratives” framing and indicates that the story continues.
